text: Comparing dialects on paper only gets you so far. Let's set up a real multi-dialect practice environment, using genuinely free tools, so you can run code on your own machine, not just read about it.

For SQL Server, you may already have a practice instance, since you know T-SQL. If not, SQL Server Developer Edition is free and full-featured, not a crippled trial. For Oracle, Oracle Database XE is a real, free, local install, or Oracle Autonomous Database Free Tier if you'd rather practice in the cloud.

MySQL Community Edition is free and open source, and it's the exact same engine used in production everywhere -- no feature-limited free tier to worry about. PostgreSQL is the same story: entirely free and open source, full stop, no edition split at all.

The cloud warehouses work a little differently. Snowflake gives you a thirty-day free trial with credits. Databricks offers a free Community Edition for running Spark SQL in a notebook. Save both of these for Chapter nine, since trial clocks are time-limited.

Once anything is installed, run its version-check query -- select at-at-version on SQL Server, select star from v-dollar-version on Oracle, select version open-paren close-paren on MySQL and Postgres. Any result back means you're ready.
Next lesson: once your environment is running, we'll talk about how to actually read each vendor's official documentation like a developer, not a DBA. See you there.
